# archestra_resource_permission_policy (Resource)

Authoritative direct grants for one object or all objects of one resource type. Declare one policy per target; inherited grants are unaffected. Destroy revokes every direct grant on the target. Updates use the last observed revision and reject concurrent changes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "archestra_resource_permission_policy" "staging" {
  resource_type = "environment"
  resource_id   = archestra_environment.staging.id
  grants = [{
    subject_type = "organization"
    subject_id   = "*"
    actions      = ["read", "use"]
  }]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `grants` (Attributes Set) Complete set of direct principal grants; an empty set revokes all direct grants. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--grants))
- `resource_id` (String) Object UUID, or * to manage the policy for all objects of this resource type.
- `resource_type` (String) API resource type whose direct grants are managed.

### Read-Only

- `effective_actions` (Set of String) Current caller's effective actions, including inherited grants.
- `id` (String) Composite resource_type/resource_id identifier.
- `owner_id` (String) Object owner, when present.
- `revision` (Number) Last observed policy revision used for optimistic concurrency.

<a id="nestedatt--grants"></a>
### Nested Schema for `grants`

Required:

- `actions` (Set of String) Actions granted to this principal.
- `subject_id` (String) Principal ID; use * for the organization principal.
- `subject_type` (String) Principal type.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import archestra_resource_permission_policy.staging environment/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001
```
